I don't know whether those people were in the Srbac Brigade or not, because this first bit of information relates exclusively to the camouflage nets, not the conversation between these three.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question, sir, is if you know the -- in which military force the 35th Srbacka Brigade was a component.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The armed force of the so-called Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General Delic, a few moments ago you made reference to a tape. Do you know what -- whether these conversations were taped? And if so, what happened to the tape?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: All conversation, all intercepts were taped. I'm 99 per cent sure that they were all delivered to the intelligence section of the 2nd Corps. That's where they were analysed and possible distribution of information was performed. If an intercept did not yield the expected results, I suppose that since we were short of resources, tapes could have been re-recorded. However, a written trace remained and it was archived in the appropriate organ of the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would ask that P02282 be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P02282 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 414.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm aware of the time. I have one remaining document. I would ask the Court's indulgence to proceed and then that would complete the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown P02899. P02899.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: While that's coming up, sir, can you tell -- remind the Trial Chamber what position you held in November 1997.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: In November 1997 until the 1st of October, 2000, I was commander of the 2nd Corps of the Federation Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you take a look, sir, at the document on the screen in front of you and tell the Trial Chamber what this document is.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The heading says: "The joint command of the Army of the Federation, administration for intelligence and security." There is no mark "strictly confidential" -- in fact, there is no strictly confidential number. The date is 14 November. It says: "Prevention of arrest of members of the former El Mujahid unit. Order." It's addressed to the 2nd Corps of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina army command and to the 7th Motorised Brigade. The typewritten signature is Rasim Delic, army general, but there is no signature in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on what the witness has just explained to the Court, in the absence of any stamp or sort of official notification of where perhaps the document may have arrived or come from, in the absence of any signature, we will be objecting to the admission of this document into evidence 1-6R7B8G9 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you think you would like to wait until the time when you are ready the object?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'll hold back, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General Delic, can you see on the upper right-hand portion of this document an indication of the method by which this document was to be sent?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: It says here that it was sent by packet communication, but you also see what I said a moment ago, that it was sent by the intelligence for intelligence and security and there is no reference number. The administration drafted this and the signature says: "Commander of the General Staff, Rasim Delic." This seems to be in a bit of a contradiction. The sender is the administration and the signature is of the general, the commander of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General Delic, do you have any recollection of ever receiving or seeing this document before?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I've already said. I haven't seen this document before. And if it had been received, it must have been received by the command of the 2nd Corps, recorded, and given a number. If it had reached the command of the 2nd Corps, it would have been received by the intelligence organ or the security organ of the 2nd Corps. It is verifiable. We have records, and I'm sure it can be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would move this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I raise the objection at this point. As I say, we can see in the top left-hand corner a place where you would normally see a number. We see from other documents that you would often find a stamp here. Obviously there's no signature on the document. And also, contrary to -- to many of the other documents we've seen, there's no sort of handwritten signature to indicate that it's been sent or received by anybody. So in the absence of any of these sort of indicia, the Defence would say -- raise serious doubts as to the reliability of this document and therefore we suggest that it shouldn't be entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The reliability, yes, understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And also, of course, what the witness has just told you, as well, his comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. Okay. You're raising doubts about its reliability but not its admissibility. That's a question of weight to be attached to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also -- it raises questions about the authenticity as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well -- yeah, but we are told here that it was sent by electronic means. How does one get a signature on an -- well, I don't know what this was. I don't know what is meant by "electronic means," anyway.. I will not go into that. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution would simply indicate, as the Presiding Judge has, that the issues raised by the Defence go more to the issue of the weight to be given to the document rather than its admissibility. With respect to the -- to the arguments concerning authenticity, there has been evidence before Your Honours about the way certain documents were handled or transmitted, and I don't want to say anything further, particularly in front of the witness with respect to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood well, the witness has finished with his comments on this document, because it has been tendered. So, first of all, we first contest the authenticity of this document. We first contest the authenticity. And if you would allow me to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just hold on. Yes, Mr. Mundis, are you -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you objecting to anything that Madam Vidovic is saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm simply raising concerns about anything that might be said in the presence of the witness, despite the fact that I'm done questioning him, other parties or the Defence or the Chamber may have questions for this witness later concerning this document, and I simply want to put on the record that perhaps the witness could be excused for the evening before anything further is said about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, you are -- okay. Mr. Delic, we are just about to finish for the day. You are excused. You may come -- come -- please come back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, III. Okay? We'll continue with your testimony tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I was saying, we first object to the authenticity of this document. The thing is every document must have a number under which it was filed. We see here: "Administration for intelligence and security," and below that, there is a line intended for the number. A number would be indicated. You are right that it was sent by electronic means, packet communications, as it was called, but every transmission by packet communications is recorded with a small note: "Sent by packet communication or sent electronically." There is no such note here and no signature and no stamp. This document would never have been sent from the General Staff. We have good reason to doubt this. Such a document does not exist. We have serious doubts about this and some other documents that the Prosecution is using here. This is not the only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem. It's not the same problem as that raised by the Defence, because on other occasions we've seen documents that were not fully comprehensive and we admitted them. But what makes me really have doubts about whether this document can be admitted is what the witness actually noted. This document seemed to be signed by Rasim Delic but was written by the administration for intelligence and security. Tomorrow we'll probably ask the witness how it could happen that a document that is sent by an administration -- by the administration in intelligence and security be signed by Rasim Delic. I beg to differ with the other people in the court. It's not a problem of weight. I think it's really a problem of admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope, Judge Lattanzi, you understand that I was not making a ruling that this is -- I was -- I was taking the words used by the counsel, who said "we doubt its reliability." So I was saying to him that if you doubt it's reliability, then we are not dealing with admissibility; we are dealing with a question of weight. And then he then said, "No, we also doubt its authenticity." So I was not saying that it -- okay? Mr. Mundis, you had -- do you have a response to Madam Vidovic's point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I -- I -- I don't believe at this point the Prosecution has anything else to add. I -- I will note that I'm not sure the basis for Mrs. Vidovic saying this document would never have been sent from the General Staff, on lines 20 to 22 on page 104. But we have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you perhaps have any other witness through whom you can book? Do you need it marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely. In the event the Chamber does not admit the document, I absolutely would like to document admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- into evidence and we'll have to call the archivist, who can tell the Chamber exactly where this document came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. In that event, it will be marked for identification. Can the it be given an exhibit number, please..

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that can be MFI 415.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I just assumed we were going to rise for the evening, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, not until you've told me that we should do so. Okay. Court adjourned until tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 21st day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.14 p.m.,
